summary: This program uses a for loop to run three laps around a track, printing each lap number, then prints a message once the loop finishes.

lines.text: All three parts of the loop's control live in the parentheses, separated by semicolons: the counter starts at 1, the loop keeps going while lap is 3 or less, and lap grows by one after each pass. Because the number of iterations is known up front, there is no need to check anything by hand the way a while loop would.
Starting at 1 and using <= 3 gives laps 1, 2, and 3. Beginners often mix these up and write < 3, which stops after two laps, or start at 0 and print a "Lap 0" nobody ran.
This is the body that repeats, and it can use lap because the counter is in scope inside the loop. The + joins the text with the current number, so each pass prints a different line.
This line sits outside the closing brace of the loop, so it runs once after the condition finally fails. Indentation alone does not decide that — the braces do.
